teams.heading: Fiji chairman says Jake White won't boot flair into touch
teams.body: Fiji's chairman says Jake White will not boot the team's flair into touch as they pursue their World Cup quest, Reuters reports. It sits alongside White's own message after Saturday's 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo: he knows Fiji play with flair, but his focus has been on control, structure and organisation. White has said he believes Fiji can be a massive force at next year's World Cup in Australia if he can assemble his best 33 players.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is a new Fiji angle rather than a retelling of the Japan result or the Nawaqanitawase pitch, both already run.

teams.heading: England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet commits future to Leicester Tigers
teams.body: Jack van Poortvliet has signed a new deal with Leicester Tigers, the 25-year-old club vice-captain who has won 27 England caps and made 118 appearances for the club since debuting in 2019. He also has an 'Elite Player Squad' contract for 2026-27. Tigers head coach Geoff Parling said: "Jack is a brilliant player, developed through our academy, and an important leader in our group." Van Poortvliet, who grew up supporting Leicester, called the decision to stay 'a pretty easy' one.

lead.why: A new contract for an England scrum-half is a fresh item, unlike the Randall and call-up pieces already run.

teams.heading: FFR orders minute’s applause before all French rugby matches for Cléa Menier
teams.body: French rugby will pay tribute this weekend to 17-year-old Cléa Menier, who died in hospital in Bordeaux after an on-field injury during an under-18 match for Union du Bassin Marmandais against Agen Agglo Rugby. The French Rugby Federation says a minute’s applause will be held before each professional and amateur match in France this weekend, and that French rugby is “deeply shaken” by her death. Her club called it “an accident”; neither the club nor the FFR has disclosed the nature of the injury.

lead.why: Alldritt's recall and the Ward and Depoortere selections have already run, so this is the strongest new France-wide item in the pack, with the federation's weekend tribute reaching every French pitch.

teams.heading: Stuart McCloskey scores as Ulster fall 34-26 to Bulls in URC
teams.body: A club story first: Stuart McCloskey scored a try and assisted another in Ulster's 34-26 United Rugby Championship defeat at Loftus Versfeld, which Planet Rugby called a "statement performance" that will put Andy Farrell on notice before the Nations Championship. McCloskey is in Farrell's 36-man squad for November. Uncapped call-up Jamie Benson rose to the Bulls' physical challenge, while Jacob Stockdale had a hit-and-miss outing.

teams.heading: Italy, winless in three matches, sit 11th of 12 on the log
teams.body: Italy have won none of their three matches in the log, sitting 11th of 12 with 37 points scored and 131 conceded, a points difference of -94. The last of those was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round three. Next on the schedule is South Africa, who beat Italy 32-14 at home in November 2025 in their last meeting.

teams.heading: Scarlets' Macs Page forced off wearing oxygen mask after a head knock
teams.body: Scarlets wing Macs Page, the uncapped 21-year-old who narrowly missed Steve Tandy's autumn squad, was forced off in their United Rugby Championship match against the Stormers in Cape Town. His head hit the turf as he tried to score, and after a stretcher was brought on he walked off receiving oxygen, with medics holding his head. Page had already crossed for his fifth try of the season, and Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies said it was only a matter of time before Wales called him up.

lead.why: A new item not yet run, and it puts an uncapped Welsh wing's scary head injury alongside his near-miss for Tandy's autumn squad.

teams.heading: Wrist injury makes Sam Prendergast a doubt for Ireland's clash with Argentina
teams.body: Ireland's Sam Prendergast is in doubt for the November clash with Argentina. RTÉ Sport reported on Saturday that his wrist injury makes him a doubt, and The Sun has since run a headline calling it a major injury scare for Ireland. The question for Los Pumas is whether Prendergast will be fit in time, and there is no fitness update in the coverage so far.

teams.heading: Wallabies flanker Rob Leota signs with Clermont until January 2027
teams.body: Rob Leota, the 21-cap Wallabies flanker, has signed with Clermont after leaving Bayonne as a free agent. The 29-year-old has committed to the Auvergne side until 31 January 2027, as Clermont wait on several injured players. Coach Christophe Urios said: "It's always difficult to find an additional player at this time of year." Leota is not among the 33 players Les Kiss named on Friday for the November Nations Championship games.

lead.why: It is the only new item on the shortlist, and it concerns a current Wallabies flanker.

teams.heading: Japan's Fiji defeat remains the men's story; no new team news today
teams.body: Today's coverage in the pack carries no new Japan men's team news, so the centenary Test is still the reference point. Fiji beat Japan 34-28 at Chichibunomiya on Saturday, a month after the Brave Blossoms had beaten them 20-15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final in September. The defeat leaves Japan 10th of 12 in the log, with Wales away in Round four next.

teams.heading: Richie Mo’unga still not ruled out as All Blacks injury list grows
teams.body: Captain Ardie Savea is one of several All Blacks now unavailable as the injury toll grows ahead of the Nations Championship campaign in Europe, joining prop Tyrel Lomax, hooker Samisoni Taukei’aho and loose forward Shannon Frizell on the sidelines. Frizell faces six weeks after rupturing his left posterior cruciate ligament, while Taukei’aho is expected to be out four to six weeks with a torn calf. The one hopeful note is flyhalf Richie Mo’unga, who has not yet been ruled out after missing both Bledisloe Cup Tests with a calf tear.

lead.why: It is the nation's own men's Test squad news, and the Mo’unga update is the part of the injury list not yet covered.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby breaks down Springboks' eight Test defeats since 2023
teams.body: South Africa have lost eight Tests since the start of 2023, and Planet Rugby has gone through the defeats to draw up what beating them requires. Across those eight, the winning side averaged 29.9 points and six of them scored 25 or more, so scoring capacity comes first. The Springboks head to Europe for the November leg of the Nations Championship, with Italy in Turin first, then France and Ireland.

lead.why: It is the only men's Test item in the pack; the other candidates are URC club matches or women's WXV coverage.
